title: Choose the check for each security symptom
objective: Pick the tool that can see each security symptom of a page and order a quick security pass.
summary: A branching deck shows three security symptoms of one page: an old library version, a missing Content-Security-Policy header, and a helper extension that asks for access to all sites. Each deep dive shows what a weak check misses and what the right check shows: Retire.js, the response headers, or the extension manifest. The deck ends with one order for a quick pass.

checkpoints.prompt: The page loads jQuery from an old file. Which check tells you whether that version has known vulnerabilities?

choices.text: Read the script tag in the Elements panel
choices.misconception: Thinks that seeing a version number also tells you whether the version is vulnerable
Confuses the policy that limits scripts with a check of the scripts themselves

checkpoints.explanation: Retire.js detects the library and its version and compares it with a list of versions that have known vulnerabilities. The Elements panel shows the tag but has no vulnerability data.

checkpoints.prompt: A helper extension asks for access to all sites. What can its content scripts do?

choices.text: Read and change the DOM of every page you open

choices.misconception: Thinks content scripts run only inside the extension user interface

choices.text: Nothing until the page allows it in its CSP
choices.misconception: Thinks the page's CSP decides which extensions may read the page

checkpoints.explanation: Match patterns in the manifest choose the pages a content script runs in. A content script reads and changes the DOM of each matching page, so access to all sites means every page.
